notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, for issue 1281, 24 September 2026. Verdict: accept. This is the largest extraction in the corpus - 739 items, 21 routes and 126 recorded mistakes for a 269-page paper - so this note is explicit about what was checked and how deeply.

SOURCE. The published text was re-fetched from the NSF public-access mirror the source block names and hashed to dd821abd...9d97: 269 pages, printed page = PDF page + 106, pp. 107-375, which matches the journal pagination. That mirror serves the published article itself, so unlike the Springer-hosted papers I reviewed yesterday the text could be read directly rather than through a proxy.

MISTAKES: ALL 126 LOCATED AND CONFIRMED. Every finding was checked at its recorded page: 99 by an automatic prose match against that page, and the remaining 27 - whose quotations are displayed formulas that no prose matcher can find - by hand, one at a time. Not one locator was wrong, which for 126 findings spread over 269 pages is itself worth recording.

EIGHT OF THE TWENTY-NINE that reach a proof or a stated result were examined in depth, and five of those I re-derived independently. E2: over O_lambda/lambda^n with n >= 2 the matrix [[lambda,1],[0,lambda]] has image of index |k|^2 while its coordinate projections have indices 1 and |k|, so no change of basis diagonalises it and 'the first part is obvious from Definition 2.6.5' does not follow. E4: condition (a) of (GI^1) asks for P(xi) invertible, which is unsatisfiable for P = 0, and the proof's step 'such pair (a,b) always exists' is where it breaks. E8: for a procyclic group acting trivially - which the proof has just established - H^1_cont(Zhat, M) = M, so the asserted vanishing is equivalent to the module vanishing and the invertibility of p^2-1 is irrelevant. E10: at N = 2 the space is q+1 points, so H^2 = 0 and the printed kernel is all of H^0, a permutation representation 1 + St that is not irreducible, exactly as the paper's own formula (C.1) implies. E13: torsion-free O_lambda[Gamma]-modules with isomorphic rationalisations need not be isomorphic. For E1, E3 and E9 I verified the printed statements and the quoted steps and the shape of the repairs, but did not re-derive the Kummer-class computation (E1) or the verification that the Shimura link fibres carry the added descent hypothesis (E9); the extraction records both as re-derived on page images, and I have said in those verdicts which part rests on its work rather than mine.

THE RECORD ITSELF IS OF UNUSUAL QUALITY. Every `printed` field is a real quotation (median 158 characters), the classifications are honest - 97 of 126 affect nothing and they genuinely do not - and several entries carry the extraction's own revisions on re-checking, including two that were promoted from gap to error (E2, E8) and one whose locator was relabelled (E10). That is what a reviewable record looks like.

CORRECTED IN PLACE. Two Part II titles were not exact prefix extensions of their parents' atlas titles, which PROTOCOL section 15 requires. 'Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles, Part II: Semistable potential maps' dropped 'nearby cycles and'; 'Selmer and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: Arithmetic level raising and Rankin-Selberg Selmer annihilators' used a shortened form of 'Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology'. Neither roadmap is proposed by any other extraction, so no coalescence with another paper is disturbed; the second one's identity in the `coalescence` block carried the same shortened title, sourced from this paper's own earlier checkpoint (PR #2181), and was updated with it. The corrected second title now matches the form PAPER-DISEGNI-LIU-24 uses for the same parent, which this session reviewed today. Separately, three item ids appeared twice inside a single route's `items` array and were de-duplicated; no item gained or lost a route, and every missing item is still routed exactly once.

ITEMS AND ROUTES. 739 items: 12 library, 32 planned, 695 missing, each missing item routed exactly once, all dependencies resolving. All stage ids cited by the 21 routes and all 27 planned targets exist in the atlas index. Twenty-one routes, all accepted: fifteen source routes, five Part IIs and one new roadmap, whose identity the coalescence block records for other extractions to join.
